title: Hybrid heat pump and gas furnace HVAC system being recommended - GreenBuildingAdvisor
summary: A 2023 Green Building Advisor forum thread on whether a new cold-climate home needs a hybrid heat pump and gas furnace.

assertions.quote: the operating cost delta is not worth the complication and cost of dealing with gas
The reality is that modern hyper heat units are no problem even in colder climate.
installers usually don’t know your heat loss and are overly conservative with the crossover point

verdicts.note: Practitioners and modelers report conservative default balance points, but systematic data on installed settings are limited.

The MA/CT metering study found impacts below assumed values partly due to other heat use, integrated controls and varying switchover temperatures, and recommends a 30F or lower switchover; how often it is set too high is not quantified.

Authors note that improved controls and lowering the switchover temperature would raise heat pump use and savings, since monitored units had spare capacity at the 10F changeover; installer practice itself is not surveyed here.

Minnesota installers commonly set the lockout around 25-35F (practice developed for non-cold-climate units), and the report says a higher setpoint would lock out the heat pump while it can still meet the load.

assertions.quote: my gas meter fee is $25/month so $300/year
On older heat pumps, the output starts falling off the cliff around that temperature.
Heat pumps spend most of the time in defrost near freezing temperature.
If the ducts were sized for a gas furnace originally you can have issues with a heat pump being able to deliver enough heat
with a heat pump you can always add a PV array to offset some of the operating costs
